conventions.convention: Reduced generalized cohomology is defined on based CW complexes via contravariant functors on based cellular maps, with a natural suspension isomorphism whose sphere coordinate is written first, and with the connector normalized as δ_f = q_f* ∘ σ rather than carried as independent structure; axioms are (H), (E) exactness of the cofiber sequence, (W) wedge, and no dimension axiom is imposed.
Pair groups come from the cofiber model h^r(B,A) := h~^r(C_{A+ to B+}) with the empty-subcomplex convention X/∅ := X_+, so h^r(B,∅) = h~^r(B_+) and the coefficient group is h^q(*) = h~^q(S^0).

Skeletal filtration normalizations X^p = ∅ for p < 0 and X^p = X for p at least dim X, with F^p h^n(X) = ker(h^n(X) to h^n(X^{p-1})) and E_1^{p,q} = h^{p+q}(X^p, X^{p-1}); convergence of the AHSS is asserted only for finite CW complexes.

Chern classes are defined by the projective-bundle relation x_E^n - a_1 x_E^{n-1} + ... + (-1)^n a_n = 0 with c_i := a_i, c_0 = 1, c_i = 0 for i > n, where x_E is the Euler class of the underlying real bundle of the tautological complex line in the complex orientation; this is the page-wide normalization c_1(L) = e(L_R) (so the tautological line on complex projective space has negative class).

Pontryagin classes are defined by p_i(E) := (-1)^i c_{2i}(E_C) with p_0 = 1 and p_i = 0 when 2i exceeds rank_R E; no orientation of the real bundle is used, since complexification is canonical and even Chern classes are conjugation invariant.

Stiefel-Whitney classes are read off the mod-two projective-bundle relation x_E^n + c_1 x_E^{n-1} + ... + c_n = 0 as w_i := c_i, with w_0 = 1 and w_i = 0 for i > n; for a line bundle w_1(L) = x_L and w(L) = 1 + x_L.

Euler classes are defined by e(ξ) = s* j* (u_ξ), the zero-section pullback of the normalized Thom class, with e(0_B) = 1; over Z the class changes sign under orientation reversal and over F_2 every bundle in the Thom scope is canonically oriented.
Unital Banach algebra means nonzero, with a unit normalized by norm exactly one; the zero algebra is excluded and nonunital objects are handled separately by unitization and by C_0-representation.

A character is a nonzero complex-linear multiplicative functional; continuity and unitality are not part of the definition (both are proved for a nonzero unital Banach algebra in ZF), and the character space initially carries only the pointwise-evaluation topology, identified with the weak-star subspace topology afterwards.

Positivity in a C*-algebra is the purely algebraic condition a = b*b; the pointwise description as nonnegativity of the transformed function is a later theorem, and unitaries are defined only in the unital case.

Unitization A^+ = A ⊕ C carries the product (a,λ)(b,μ) = (ab + λb + μa, λμ) and the quotient character χ_∞(a,λ) = λ; the minimal C*-norm ‖L_a + λI‖ is imposed only for a nonzero genuinely nonunital A, and no norm is defined before that theorem.

An approximate unit is a net over a nonempty directed set of self-adjoint positive contractions with ‖e_i a - a‖ and ‖a e_i - a‖ tending to 0; a star-homomorphism is proper when it carries every approximate unit of the source to an approximate unit of the target, and a continuous map of spaces is proper when inverse images of compacta are compact.

In the Gelfand-Kolmogorov block C(X) means all continuous real-valued functions (unbounded, not a Banach algebra), and a z-filter is a family of zero sets containing X, omitting ∅, closed under finite intersections and upward closed inside the family of all zero sets; z-ultrafilters are the maximal ones.

Stone space means compact Hausdorff with a clopen basis (the clopen-basis form, not the connected-component characterisation); the ultrafilter space Ult(B) is by definition only the space generated by the sets [b] = {U : b in U}, with compactness and Hausdorffness supplied later by theorems under AC.

load_bearing.statement: A reduced generalized cohomology theory on based CW complexes: contravariant functors on based CW complexes and based cellular maps, natural suspension isomorphisms σ: h~^n(X) to h~^{n+1}(ΣX) with the sphere coordinate written first, connecting maps normalized by δ_f = q_f* ∘ σ, and axioms (H) homotopy invariance, (E) exactness of the cofiber sequence, (W) the wedge axiom; no dimension axiom and no coefficient restriction.

CW-pair cohomology theories with axioms (H), (LES), (Ex) and (Add) and no dimension axiom, and reduced generalized cohomology theories, determine one another naturally: h^n(X,A) := h~(C_i) with the convention X/∅ = X_+, and h~^n(Y) := h^n(Y,*), the two constructions being canonically inverse with connecting maps agreeing.

For a finite CW complex X with supplied characteristic maps and cell orientations, the first skeletal groups E_1^{p,q} = h^{p+q}(X^p, X^{p-1}) satisfy natural isomorphisms E_1^{p,q} ≅ C^p_cell(X; h^q(*)), commuting with cellular maps and with morphisms of reduced theories.

For a finite CW complex X and a reduced generalized cohomology theory h~ with associated pair theory h there is a cohomological spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = h^{p+q}(X^p, X^{p-1}), E_2^{p,q} ≅ H^p(X; h^q(*)), d_r: E_r^{p,q} to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}, natural in cellular maps and in morphisms of theories, whose stable page is the associated graded E_∞^{p,q} ≅ F^p h^{p+q}(X)/F^{p+1}h^{p+q}(X) of the skeletal filtration.

Let E to B be a numerable complex rank-n bundle with n at least 1 over a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CW complex, with projective bundle P(E) and x in H^2(P(E);Z) the tautological class. For R = Z and for every field F_p, H*(P(E);R) is a free H*(B;R)-module with basis 1, x_R, ..., x_R^{n-1}; integrally the relation x^n - a_1x^{n-1} + ... + (-1)^n a_n = 0 has unique coefficients and the monic relation generates every polynomial relation.

By the projective bundle theorem there are unique classes a_i in H^{2i}(B;Z) with x_E^n - a_1x_E^{n-1} + ... + (-1)^n a_n = 0 in H^{2n}(P(E);Z); the Chern classes are c_i(E) := a_i, with c_0(E) = 1 and c_i(E) = 0 for i > n, and for a complex line c_1(L) = e(L_R) in the complex orientation.

For a numerable real rank-n bundle E over an admissible base with tautological class x_E in H^1(P(E);F_2), there are unique classes c_i with x_E^n + c_1x_E^{n-1} + ... + c_n = 0; w_i(E) := c_i, with w_0 = 1 and w_i = 0 for i > n, and for a line bundle w_1(L) = x_L with w(L) = 1 + x_L.

For an R-oriented numerable real rank-n bundle ξ the Euler class is e(ξ) = s* j* (u_ξ), the zero-section pullback of the normalized Thom class; for rank zero e(0_B) = 1, over F_2 every real bundle in the Thom scope is canonically oriented, and over Z reversing the orientation negates the class.

For a real bundle E the Pontryagin classes are p_i(E) := (-1)^i c_{2i}(E_C) in H^{4i}(B;Z), with p_0 = 1 and p_i = 0 whenever 2i exceeds rank_R E; the definition requires no orientation and the odd Chern classes of a complexified real bundle are two-torsion.

A character on an associative complex algebra A is a nonzero complex-linear multiplicative map A to C, with continuity and preservation of a unit deliberately not assumed; the character space Δ(A) carries the pointwise-evaluation topology, and only later is it identified with the weak-star subspace topology of the dual ball.
Assume AC. For a nonzero unital commutative complex C*-algebra A the Gelfand transform Γ: A to C(Δ(A)), Γ(a) = â with â(χ) = χ(a), is an isometric unital *-isomorphism onto C(Δ(A)).

Assume AC. For a nonzero genuinely nonunital C*-algebra A, the operator norm ‖(a,λ)‖ := ‖L_a + λI‖ on the algebraic unitization A^+ is a C*-norm extending the norm of A and making A^+ a unital C*-algebra in which A is a closed two-sided *-ideal of codimension one; any C*-norm on A^+ extending the norm of A equals it.

Assume AC. For every commutative C*-algebra A, possibly nonunital and possibly zero, the Gelfand transform Γ: A to C_0(Δ(A)), Γ(a)(φ) = φ(a), is an isometric *-isomorphism onto C_0(Δ(A)), Δ(A) being locally compact Hausdorff in the weak-star topology.

Assume AC. For a unital complex Banach algebra A, a in A and f holomorphic on an open U containing the nonempty compact spectrum σ_A(a), one picks an admissible finite polygonal cycle Γ with winding number 1 on σ_A(a) and 0 off U and sets f(a) := (1/2πi) ∫_Γ f(z) R(z,a) dz; the value depends only on the germ of f near the spectrum and is independent of the admissible cycle.

A unital complex Banach algebra is a nonzero complex vector space with associative bilinear multiplication and a submultiplicative complete norm, possessing a unit 1 with 1a = a1 = a for all a and normalized by ‖1‖ = 1; the zero algebra is excluded by the definition.

concerns.concern: The identification of the first stable Postnikov invariant of ku with the integral operation Sq^3_Z is carried by the single source input [F5] (Adams, Stable Homotopy and Generalised Homology, Proposition 16.6, opening at printed p. 391, with the argument continuing on pp. 392-393 through a mod-two module calculation that is not reproduced). The facts that the third space can be taken to be SU and that H^6(SU;Z) = 0 are source-supplied rather than locally computed. The local deductions I checked are consistent with their suppliers: thm-postnikov-towers-exist-for-connected-cw-complexes (opened) really does give attaching cells of dimension at least n+2, so (P_5Y, Y) has no relative cells below dimension seven, and the section-pullback injectivity in step 3.1 is a correct left-inverse argument. The residual risk is the unreproduced source computation, not the local chain; severity reflects that the item itself declares this limitation.

The headline claim d_3 = Sq^3_Z = β_Z Sq^2 ρ_2 with Bott-periodic translates on all even coefficient rows inherits the same unreproduced Adams input as its supplier lem-ku-representability-and-skeletal-postnikov-d-three-comparison, and the periodic translates are asserted uniformly rather than derived row by row. The d_2 = 0 clause is immediate because the odd coefficient rows vanish, and the naturality-to-a-point and disconnected-component arguments check out. Step-7 obligation: decide whether the source-level warrant for the d_3 identification is acceptable without reproducing Adams pp. 392-393.

The source record states that the Gillman-Henriksen-Jerison endpoint was inaccessible in this run and that the proof supplied is a local alternative recorded in the Batch 4 coverage ledger, so the adjudicator must treat the local text as the warrant. I read the local proof and it is complete: Z[M] is a z-filter, upward closure is obtained from 1 = m + ah with w = f^2 + m^2 everywhere positive, separation of z-ultrafilters gives maximality of M_U, and the two assignments are inverse; the ZF claim is supported. The same source-access limitation appears in lem-zero-set-ultrafilters-and-stone-cech-points, thm-gelfand-kolmogorov-for-rings-of-continuous-functions and ex-gelfand-kolmogorov-recovers-beta-x-not-x, whose local proofs I also read and found complete given the AC-declared βX supplier (the beta-X/z-ultrafilter bijection proof uses only one nonemptiness selection from a finite-intersection-property intersection).

This recorded-not-proved remark, together with rem-gerlits-nagy-remains-selection-principle-theory and rem-linear-dugundji-extension-remains-topological, states externally sourced equivalences whose exact statements were not full-text verified in this run and whose stronger compact-open continuous linear-operator form of Dugundji is explicitly not established; each item's external_dependency block says the catalogue target stays Recorded and that the statement is used in no proof. The Step-7 obligation is to keep these non-load-bearing and to check that no later consumer cites them as suppliers, since their presence on a page of proved items is a presentation risk rather than a mathematical one.

seams_checked.note: Declared requires edge with no citing text anywhere. I searched all 40 items of the Banach pair for citations of the 21 items listed on that group-e page and for the page id itself: there is no item-level dependency and no prose use. The run's unified ledger research/phase-2-remaining-27-cross-batch-dependencies.json contains no edge whose supplier lies on that page and whose consumer is in batch 4 (its only outgoing edge is into batch 12), and the batch-4 cross-batch file has no such edge either. The compact-operator material the page actually uses (K(X), the ideal property, Atkinson, the Calkin algebra) is cited from compact-operators-and-riesz-schauder-theory, not from the trace-class page. Hence no citing text overstates or understates the cited page; the declared requirement is page metadata only and is non-load-bearing, which is the observation to carry into adjudication.
